text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Conservative Party's European Parliament members reject MP Ben Zyskowicz's views that the European Parliament does not represent democracy and could be abolished.
- Quality of Finnish construction work is still poor. Tight contract schedules make Finns build fast and cheaply, sector representatives say.
- Crimes of racism have no organised base in Finland, head of Security Police Seppo Nevala said. @
- Regardless of whether or not Finland joins EMU, inflation should be kept low, says Lauri Ihalainen, chairman of the Central Organization of Finnish Trade Unions, SAK.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Pohjola's advisor in Suomi-Salama buy London's Fox-Pitt, Kelton estimates the acquisition of Salama will cost 537 million markka, and will have no major impact on the value of Pohjola's share.
- Editor-in-chief of Swedish business newspaper Dagens Industri Hasse Olsson says there is no room for two business papers in a single European country. @
- Morgan Stanley executive Robert Sargent says neither Nokia nor Ericsson meet the criteria that the investment bank sets on stocks it includes in its own portfolio.
AAMULEHTI
- Breaking up Finnish cooperative dairy products group Valio and making regional dairies independent would lead to fierce price competition, sector representative says.
- Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners MTK harshly criticised the environment ministry's Natura 2000 programme. @
AAMULEHTI
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says employment of women should pick up with general economic recovery.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Head of Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) Lauri Ihalainen said conditions for employment should not be spoiled by excessive salary demands in the next round of pay talks, calls for a two-year, moderate agreement. @
DEMARI
- Two industrial actions threaten the Helsinki area: public transport workers due to strike on Wednesday and energy department employees have also obtained permission to strike.
HUVUDSTADSBLADET
- Trade unions should not get involved in the EMU debate, Finnish Communist Party leader Yrjo Hakanen says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
